findings.finding: The upper front wall beside the windows carries pale, wavy, chip-like colour boundaries not resolved as corresponding edges in the source. In the native focus crop, these boundaries are conspicuous in colour while largely disappearing in grayscale. Geometry and source grain are closely retained, but the chromatic pattern still suggests newly drawn peeling/plaster layers. This is a specific material-surface preservation failure, not a rejection of an ordinary provisional hue.
Four upper front windows, lower gate, entrance and lower window, chimneys, roof edge, annex, major damage patches, ivy, tree, grass, leaning board and pole remain aligned and recognizable.
Source plaque stays similarly soft; its digits are not promoted to confirmed identity. No newly sharpened transcription is credited.
Ochre plaster, brown timber, gray-green gate, tile red and greenery are distinguishable and treated as provisional. The residual upper-wall flake-shaped colour boundaries are the rejection reason.

Matched dimensions and very close grayscale structure support the visual preservation findings but are not a visual pass or proof of historical colours. Chroma-only material patterns must be judged in colour.

data.method: Pillow grayscale BT601 coefficients on stored nonlinear RGB; no geometric registration or source/output changes. Comparison is diagnostic, not a visual verdict.
